page.layout: One page of text in one column. Running head at top left, page number at top right. Under the running head, a centred italic title line. Then a list of ten italic questions, a centred heading for question 1, and the running text in paragraphs. One margin note on the right beside the line "Inspira-". Catchword "hunc" at the bottom right.

main_text.l: De Spiritu sancto.
Quæstiones præcipuæ.
1. Quid nomen Spiritus significet.
2. Quis, & quid sit Spiritus sanctus.
3. Quodnam Spiritus sancti sit officium.
4. A quo detur Spiritus sanctus, & quare.
5. Quibus detur.
6. Quomodo detur, & accipiatur.
7. Quomodo retineatur.
8. An, & quomodo amittatur.
9. Quare sit necessarius.
10. Unde agnoscatur eius habitatio in nobis.
1. Quid nomen Spiritus significet.
Nomen Spiritus aliquando pro causa sumitur,
aliquando pro effectu. Quando pro causa accipitur, signi-

aliter & personaliter est spiritus, hoc est, incorporeus, sine
dimensionibus corporum, indivisibilis. 2. Angeli quoq;
& ij vel boni, vel mali, sunt hac ratione Spiritus. 3. E-
odem modo Spiritus dicuntur hominum animæ. Inspira-
vit in faciem eius spiraculum vitæ: id est, immisit spiritum.
Quando nomen spiritus pro effectu capitur, significat.
1. Aerem impulsum. 2. Ipsam impulsionem, & motum aeris. 3.
Ventum ac vapores impellentes. 4. Effectus aut motus spiritua-
les, bonos vel malos. Sic Spiritus timoris, & contrà Spiritus
Principum, id est, fortitudo: item Spiritus fornicationis.
5. Spiritus novus significat dona Spiritus sancti. Dicitur au-
tem Spiritus à spirando, sicut πνευμα ἀ πνεω[?].

tantem, ac moventem: nempe tertiam personam Deitatis,
quæ efficax est in mentibus ac voluntatibus homi-

page.notes: Printed page 457. The running head is "DE HOMINIS LIBERAT." and the centred title "De Spiritu sancto." sits beneath it. The catchword "hunc" is at the lower right and is not repeated in the text. The margin note "Gen. 2. 7." is beside the line "Inspira-" and is placed after that word. The Greek "πνευμα ἀ πνεω" is printed in small type and the accents are uncertain, so it is marked [?]. Italic and roman boundaries in some phrases are read from the scan and may not be exact. Printed "u" in "Inspiravit", "indiuisibilis" and "inuisibilis" is read as consonant v as the rules require.
